name: Zero Orientation-Square Defect Characterizes Dismantlable Ampleness
scope: For every nonempty finite partial cube $H$, $\mu(H)=0$ if and only if $H$ is dismantlable ample. For a vertex $a$, $\mu(H,a)=0$ if and only if $H$ corner-peels to $a$.
proof: Every acyclically oriented square has one or two sources. Consequently the score counts missing opposite vertices of outgoing edge pairs and the extra sources of squares, so it is nonnegative. Score zero makes every topological order a metric-elimination order and hence a corner peeling; a corner order conversely supplies every required opposite vertex and gives every square one source. Requiring $a$ to be a sink makes the topological order end at $a$.
